title: Microsoft 365 Backup: Full Workload Backup policies for SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange
notes: claim 96: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page

claims.claim: The pricing page lists no separate Full Workload Backup meter or charge.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Full Workload Backup pricing license separate charge. Opened backup-pricing and backup-overview on Learn; the pricing page lists the protected-content meter, not a separate Full Workload Backup charge.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup Administrators can manage all three workloads and the entire tool.
claims.quote: We have also introduced a new dedicated role for this tool, the Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator, that can control the entire tool.

claims.claim: Exclusions are added by following the listed path from Exclude more directly to Save.
claims.quote:
4. Select Exclude more.
5. Upload a CSV file containing the protection units that you want to exclude.
6. Select Save.
claims.fix: Replace the path in controls[1].ui and its rendered table cell with 'Microsoft 365 Backup > Backup policies > Full Workload Backup policy > View details > Excluded > Exclude more > Upload a CSV file containing the protection units to exclude > Save'. The cited Learn procedure requires the CSV upload between Exclude more and Save.

claims.claim: The notification settings are at Microsoft 365 Backup > Email notifications in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Go to the Email notifications option on the Microsoft 365 Backup home page.

claims.claim: Update-MgSolutionBackupRestoreEmailNotificationSetting -IsEnabled implements who is told when backup policies change.
claims.quote:
Existing properties that aren't included in the request body maintain their previous values or are recalculated based on changes to other property values.
isEnabled: Indicates whether notifications are enabled.
recipients: Specifies the recipients who receive the notifications.
claims.fix: Replace the call in controls[2].api and its rendered table cell with "Update-MgSolutionBackupRestoreEmailNotificationSetting -IsEnabled -AdditionalEvents restoreAndPolicyUpdates -Recipients @{Role='custom'; CustomRecipients=@(@{Email='<recipient-email>'})}". The recipient placeholder must represent the intended notification list; repeat the email entry for additional intended recipients. The existing cmdlet reference documents both parameters and the recipients hashtable; https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/emailnotificationssetting-update?view=graph-rest-1.0 documents restoreAndPolicyUpdates and the complete request.

claims.claim: Global admins can enable email notifications and update the notification list.
claims.quote: Global admins and Microsoft 365 Backup admins can turn on this feature and update the notification list at any time.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup admins can enable email notifications and update the notification list.
claims.quote: Global admins and Microsoft 365 Backup admins can turn on this feature and update the notification list at any time.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Creating or modifying backup policies is a routine notification event in the general Backup notification feature.
claims.quote:
Routine events
- Creating or modifying backup policies
- Initiating or completing restores

claims.claim: Routine notifications require opting in rather than being included by default.
claims.quote: By default, recipients are notified only about potentially harmful events, but you can also opt in to receive notifications for routine events.

claims.claim: Removing protection units from backup policies is listed as a potentially harmful notification event.
claims.quote:
Potentially harmful events
- Disabling Microsoft 365 Backup
- Pausing billing due to issues or admin action
- Removing protection units from backup policies

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Full Workload Backup exclusion list edits turn off email notifications. Read Learn backup-setup and backup-view-edit-policies; generic policy modification/removal events are listed, but exclusion-list edits are not explicitly mapped to an email event.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly stated whether turning off Full Workload Backup sends an email notification.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Full Workload Backup exclusion list edits turn off email notifications. Read Learn backup-setup and backup-view-edit-policies; disabling the whole Backup service is listed, but turning off Full Workload Backup is not explicitly mapped to an email event.

claims.claim: Full Workload Backup provides a single policy for a selected SharePoint, OneDrive or Exchange workload.
claims.quote: a new capability that allows admins to quickly protect an entire workload (SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange) with a single policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Protection covers eligible units except those in custom policies, on the exclusion list, or being permanently deleted from Backup.
claims.quote: Full Workload Backup automatically protects all eligible protection units that aren't already included in a custom backup policy, added to the exclusion list, or in the process of being permanently deleted from Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says newly created items join backup coverage automatically on subsequent runs.
claims.quote: Newly created artifacts will be included in backup coverage automatically on subsequent runs.

claims.claim: Full Workload Backup can be enabled independently for each workload.
claims.quote: You can enable Full Workload Backup independently for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange.

claims.claim: Existing custom backup policies continue unchanged.
claims.quote: Other “custom” backup policies continue to work without changes

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Custom backup policies take precedence over Full Workload Backup.
claims.quote: Custom backup policies always take precedence over Full Workload Backup.

claims.claim: A unit in an active or paused custom policy is not protected by the Full Workload Backup policy.
claims.quote: A protection unit that's already included in a custom backup policy (in an active or paused state) will not be protected by the Full Workload Backup policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support

claims.quote: If you attempt to add a protection unit that is already protected by Full Workload Backup to a custom backup policy, the protection unit will be moved to that custom policy automatically

claims.claim: Moving a protected unit from Full Workload Backup to a custom policy leaves no gap in recovery-point coverage.
claims.quote: the protection unit will be moved to that custom policy automatically, with no gap in its recovery point coverage.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Billing is based on the size of content once it is added to backup protection.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup charges you based on the size of the following content once it's added to backup protection.

claims.claim: Protected storage charges include SharePoint and OneDrive second-stage recycle-bin content.
claims.quote: Deleted content in SharePoint sites' and OneDrive accounts' second-stage recycle bin (also known as site collection recycle bin).

claims.claim: Protected mailbox size includes associated online archives when used.
claims.quote: Size of the live user or shared mailbox plus their associated online archives if those are being used.

claims.quote:

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Linking an Azure subscription for pay-as-you-go billing is a service setup step.

claims.claim: The newer billing experience offers budget alerts.

claims.claim: Reaching 100% of a billing-policy budget does not stop service or billing.
claims.quote: Reaching 100% of your budget doesn't stop the service or billing.

claims.claim: PowerShell or Microsoft 365 usage reports can supply storage-size information for estimates.
claims.quote:
Sizes of live data, and deleted data for your SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Exchange mailboxes can be calculated using two different methods:
- PowerShell commands or scripts
- Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports

claims.claim: Only tenant-level admins can create and manage backups.
claims.quote: Only tenant-level admins can create and manage backups using Microsoft 365 Backup for their users.

claims.claim: The administrator's role determines which Backup workloads they can manage.
claims.quote: It's important to note that your admin role determines which products you can manage with Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.claim: Excluding or removing a protected unit leaves existing backups available according to its retention settings.
claims.quote:
Regardless, existing backups for that protection unit will remain for its defined retention period.
Your existing backups stay available for restore based on your retention settings

claims.claim: Removing a unit from the Full Workload Backup policy adds it to the exclusion list.
claims.quote: When you remove a protection unit from the Full Workload Backup policy, it's added to the policy's exclusion list.

claims.claim: Removal from Full Workload Backup stops new backups for that unit.
claims.quote: This keeps Full Workload Backup from automatically re-protecting it again, and no new backups are taken for it.

claims.claim: Turning off Full Workload Backup removes its policy.
claims.quote:
After Full Workload Backup is turned off:
- The Full Workload Backup policy is removed.

claims.claim: Units protected only by the policy move to Removed items when Full Workload Backup is turned off.
claims.quote: Protection units associated only with the Full Workload Backup policy move to the Removed items tab.

claims.claim: After shutdown, new backups stop until affected units join a custom policy or Full Workload Backup is re-enabled.
claims.quote: New backups will not be taken, unless and until the protection unit(s) are added to a custom policy or the Full Workload Backup policy is re-enabled.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup supports user mailboxes.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup supports both user mailboxes and shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup supports shared mailboxes.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup supports both user mailboxes and shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup does not support room mailboxes.
claims.quote: Other Exchange recipient types, including room mailboxes and group mailboxes, aren't supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup does not support group mailboxes.
claims.quote: Other Exchange recipient types, including room mailboxes and group mailboxes, aren't supported.

claims.claim: Some legacy SharePoint site templates are unsupported.
claims.quote: Some legacy SharePoint site templates are not supported by Microsoft 365 Backup.

claims.claim: The published scale limit is 1,000,000 items per workload.
claims.quote: Items per workload: up to 1,000,000 items per workload.

claims.claim: The published scale limit is 100 backup policies per workload.
claims.quote: Policies per workload: up to 100 backup policies per workload.

claims.claim: The published scale limit is 100,000 items per backup policy.
claims.quote: Items per policy: up to 100,000 items per backup policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs organisations needing higher scale to contact Microsoft.
claims.quote: If your organization needs to protect data beyond these limits, contact Microsoft to discuss options for a higher scale.

claims.where: Governance controls: turning the policy off
claims.claim: The shutdown entry point is Backup policies > Full Workload Backup policy > Turn off Full Workload Backup.
claims.quote:

Select Turn off Full Workload Backup either from the command bar or the policy details pane.

claims.claim: The beta REST create reference does not list protectionMode in its request-body table.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph beta create sharePointProtectionPolicy protectionMode request body. claims.quote: When set to fullServiceBackup, the entire workload is backed up and specific sites can be excluded using exclusion units.

claims.claim: The notice identifies administrators managing Microsoft 365 Backup policies as an affected audience.

claims.quote:
When Full Workload Backup is active and you remove a protection unit from a custom backup policy, choose one of the following options:

- Move to Full Workload Backup

claims.claim: End users get no new experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup Full Workload Backup end users no impact user experience transparent. Read backup-setup, backup-overview and backup-view-edit-policies. They describe admin management, not an explicit assurance that end users get no new experience.
claims.fix: Remove 'and end users get no new experience' from the impact rationale. Keep the low impact judgement and its documented premise that the notice identifies administrators managing Backup policies as an affected audience.
